summary: Former Forest Service lookout on Bald Butte, Hood River County: an 80-foot tower of 1941, cut to about 41 feet in 1944, gone by 1972.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a timber tower
facts.status_note: Removed by 1972 per the register, Rex's page, firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers; no source describes what remains on the site

staffing.status: Staffed 95 days in 1941; one first report in 1965; no later staffing in these sources

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mount Hood National Forest)

access.note: Vehicles reach the site by Forest Road 17 and a powerline corridor; the Oregon Hikers guide also notes frequent ATV use

visit.trail_note: Oregon Hikers lists a moderate 8.2-mile route that climbs through open meadows to the former lookout site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1933 newspaper item announced a new tower. The register and firelookout.com give 1941 for an 80-foot tower, and Rex's page gives a 40-foot replacement in 1952. The sources do not say whether the 1933 plan produced the 1941 tower, and they disagree on the 1944 cut and the 1952 replacement.

notes_for_editor: No source we read describes what remains on the site today, so the story says so. Build and removal dates disagree: 1941 build and 1944 cut (register, firelookout.com) against a 1933 plan and a 1952 40-foot replacement (Rex). Height kept at 12.2 m from the record, which matches the 40-foot figure in Rex and Oregon Hikers; the register and firelookout.com say 41 feet after 1944. Elevation: the register gives 3,779 ft (1,152 m), which matches the record; an Oregon Hikers search snippet shows 3,070 ft, not read in full. The Oregon Hikers coordinates (45.5502, -121.5334) sit about 1.5 km north of the record point. A cherylhill.net 2018 post titled Bald Butte (41-foot timber tower, a 1959 replacement that 'still stands') names no forest and its dates do not match this site; it was excluded, and a 2022 blog post on an Ochoco National Forest Bald Butte suggests it is a different site. The editor may want to confirm before using it.
